plan.title: WGCNA co-expression modules, case vs control blood
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12000 x 121 raw Salmon gene-level counts across 120 whole-blood samples (60 case, 60 control), single batch, unpaired. The research question asks which co-expression modules the genes form across all 120 samples and which modules track case/control status — this is a WGCNA co-expression + module-trait association question, not a differential expression question, though DE-style QC and normalization steps are the standard precursor the knowledge base grounds for this exact situation (R-0033, R-0002/R-0029, R-0026). Track T1 does sample-structure QC and low-count filtering on the raw counts; track T2 runs the signed WGCNA network (soft-threshold by scale-free fit, dynamic tree cut modules, module eigengenes) and correlates each module eigengene against case/control status (and any other sample-level covariates in metadata.csv), ranking genes within significant modules by module membership (kME) to name hub genes; track T3 optionally contextualizes the trait-associated modules against MSigDB Hallmark / GO gene sets (both staged for human) so a module's function has an independent annotation beyond its member list. A final report step assembles the full co-expression report per R-0151 (module sizes, eigengene-trait correlations with adjusted p-values, hub genes, reproducibility record). Caveat carried through the plan: WGCNA on a two-group cohort of 60 vs 60 gives a module-trait correlation that is an association within this cohort, not a validated pathway or a causal claim, and with 12000 genes across 121 columns (metadata reports 120 rows for 121 count columns — an off-by-one the QC step must reconcile explicitly before any module-trait test).

steps.method: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes
WGCNA signed network, dynamic tree cut, module eigengenes
Co-expression module report with eigengene-trait correlations
